candidate_revisions.statement: Assume the finite mixing statement at revision 2 and the actual-source budget inputs in mathematics.md. With the stated m,N,K,eta scales, the normalized nonbaseline geometry, retained mass and squared phase costs are O(eta^-7*ell^-2*log(ell)), O(eta^-4/ell) and O(eta^-19*ell^-4*log(ell)^2). For eta=ell^-q they vanish when 0<q<4/19, permitting 2A<q<4/19 for any fixed 0<A<2/19. For eta=kappa*R^-2, the endpoint R=c_R*ell^(2/19)*(log(ell))^(-1/19) leaves a phase bound O(kappa^-19*c_R^38), so a sufficiently small c_R can meet a fixed budget after kappa is fixed. With log power p>1/19 that phase bound vanishes for every fixed positive c_R. These are conditional budget conclusions, not a theorem about actual Jensen roots.
